h1: Traffic Warrant Recall & Lift in El Paso, Texas
intro: A missed court date on a traffic ticket in El Paso turns into an arrest warrant fast. Attorney Robert Navar files an appearance, asks the court to recall the warrant, and in most cases has it lifted within 24–48 hours — no jail, no bondsman, no walking into the courthouse.

sections.heading: How a Traffic Ticket Becomes a Warrant in El Paso
paragraphs: Every citation in El Paso carries an appearance date, usually 10 to 20 days after the stop. If you do not pay, plead, or have a lawyer appear by that date, the court treats the silence as a failure to appear. El Paso Municipal Court then issues an arrest warrant on the original ticket and files a second Class C charge for the failure to appear itself. A single $200 speeding ticket quietly becomes two cases and a warrant.

The same thing happens in the Justice of the Peace precincts, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony. Each court runs its own warrant list, and many people in El Paso County carry warrants in two or three courts at once without knowing it.

The warrant does not go away with time. It stays active until the case is resolved, and the court also reports the unresolved case to the Texas Department of Public Safety, which leads to an OMNI hold on your driver's license renewal.

sections.heading: Recall vs. Lift vs. Posting a Cash Bond
paragraphs: People use "recall" and "lift" interchangeably, and in practice both mean the same thing: the judge signs an order withdrawing the warrant so police no longer have authority to arrest you on it. The important difference is how the warrant gets withdrawn, because the three routes cost very different amounts of money and stress.

You can walk into the court and post a cash bond for the full fine on every case, which often means several hundred dollars up front just to get a new court date. You can wait to be arrested and go through booking at the county jail. Or you can hire an attorney to file a notice of appearance and a motion to recall, which lets the court reset the case without a bond and without you going anywhere near the jail.

sections.heading: What a Warrant Recall Costs and How Fast It Works
paragraphs: Our pricing is flat and posted. The underlying ticket is $59 in El Paso Municipal Court or $69 in JP, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. On top of that, the warrant work is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional warrant. So a driver with one ticket and one warrant in Municipal Court pays $94 total to have the warrant recalled and the ticket fought — far less than posting a cash bond or paying a bondsman.

Once you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file the notice of appearance and the request to recall the same business day. In El Paso Municipal Court the judge typically signs the recall within 24 to 48 hours; the smaller courts can take a few days depending on when their judge sits. We confirm with the clerk that the warrant is out of the system before we tell you it is clear.

From that point the case is simply an open ticket on a pretrial docket, and we handle it like any other citation: we push for a dismissal or deferred disposition so the original violation never becomes a conviction. In most cases you never go to court.

sections.heading: Warrant Roundup Season and Traffic Stops That Turn Into Arrests
paragraphs: Every spring, El Paso Municipal Court and courts across Texas take part in the statewide warrant roundup. Courts publish notice, then officers actively serve outstanding Class C warrants — at homes, at workplaces, and through extra traffic enforcement. If you have an old ticket warrant, the weeks before the roundup are the time to deal with it, because the amnesty period usually lets you resolve the case without the arrest that follows once the roundup starts.

The rest of the year, the most common way a warrant surfaces is an ordinary traffic stop. An officer on Mesa Street or Loop 375 runs your license, the warrant appears, and a routine stop for a speeding ticket ends with handcuffs, a tow, and a night at the county jail. Warrants also show up on employment background checks and when you try to renew your license and discover the OMNI hold.

We wrote more about the process in our post on getting El Paso warrants lifted and about what an effective warrant lawyer does. The short version: it is far cheaper and faster to recall a warrant on your own schedule than on the officer's.

sections.heading: Warrants From Other El Paso County Courts
paragraphs: We recall traffic warrants in every court in the county: El Paso Municipal Court, all Justice of the Peace precincts, and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton municipal courts. Fort Bliss soldiers and drivers from Canutillo are a large part of our warrant practice, and we regularly handle cases for clients who have since moved away and cannot appear in person.

Because each court keeps its own list, the first step is always the same: find every warrant. Our free lookup form takes your name and date of birth, and our office checks each court and reports back what we find, which court it is in, and the fee to clear it. Se habla español.

sections.heading: What to Do Today If You Think You Have a Warrant
paragraphs: Do not drive to the courthouse to "ask" — if the warrant is active you can be arrested at the window. Do not pay the ticket online either, because paying is a guilty plea that puts a conviction on your DPS record. Fill out the lookup form or call us, and let us file the recall. Once the warrant is gone, the case is just a ticket, and tickets are what we fight every day.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. Consultations are free, and the sooner you call, the sooner you can stop looking in the rearview mirror.

faqs.q: How fast can you get a traffic warrant lifted in El Paso?
faqs.a: In El Paso Municipal Court, usually within 24 to 48 hours of hiring us. Smaller courts like Horizon City and Socorro may take a few days depending on when their judge is available. We confirm directly with the clerk before telling you the warrant is clear.

faqs.q: Will I have to go to jail or see a bondsman?
faqs.a: No. An attorney appearance lets the court recall a Class C traffic warrant without an arrest, a cash bond, or a bail bondsman. You stay home, we file the paperwork, and the court resets your case to a normal docket.

faqs.q: What does a warrant recall cost?
faqs.a: The warrant work is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional warrant. That is added to the flat ticket fee of $59 in El Paso Municipal Court or $69 in JP and the smaller city courts. Court fines, if any, are separate and depend on how the case resolves.

faqs.q: Does recalling the warrant make the ticket go away?
faqs.a: No, it reopens the ticket so it can be fought. After the recall we handle the original citation and the failure-to-appear charge together, working for a dismissal or deferred disposition. See our failure to appear page for how both cases resolve.

faqs.q: I moved away from El Paso. Can you still clear my warrant?
faqs.a: Yes. We represent clients who now live elsewhere in Texas, out of state and overseas. Since our office appears for you, you do not need to travel back to El Paso for a Class C traffic warrant.

faqs.q: How do I find out if I have a warrant in El Paso?
faqs.a: Use our free ticket and warrant lookup. We check El Paso Municipal Court, the JP precincts and the area city courts and tell you exactly what is outstanding, where, and what it will cost to clear.
